subject: FluxHealth economic review & pricing options
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tom Barlow <tom@fluxhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: FluxHealth economic review & pricing options

Tom — great to meet earlier. Quick written recap from today’s discovery so we have aligned next steps and a starting econ posture. Attaching the usage estimate workbook and two shallow pricing scenarios. (attachment: flux_poc_usage_estimates.xlsx) (attachment: redwood_pricing_scenarios.pdf)

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary workload: clinical triage + summary generation for patient messages. Peak seq lengths ~1.2k tokens; average turn ~280 tokens.
- Traffic profile: expect a 3-month pilot, then ramp; estimated monthly token consumption ranges: low 18M / mid 36M / high 62M tokens.
- Success signals: 75% reduction in human triage time and accuracy within +/-2% of clinician review.

FluxHealth budget guardrails you shared: $2k–$6k/mo for pilot, target $/1M tokens roughly in the $40–$70 range depending on latency/service SLAs. You asked about startup incentives + committed-use options.

Proposed initial options (high level):
1) Pay-as-you-go (no commitment): $85 per 1M tokens (baseline, hosted), predictable low-touch.
2) Starter discounted band (3mo commit): $60 per 1M tokens for first 3 months if FluxHealth signs 3mo POC for projected mid-case volumes (36M/mo), includes 10% free token buffer.
3) Committed 12-mo (multi-year pathing): $45 per 1M tokens with 12-mo commitment on forecasted 36M/mo + monthly overage buckets. Additional 10% rebate if FluxHealth commits to a 24-mo renewal within the 12-mo period.

Target questions for you and procurement so I can finalize numbers for legal:
- Can you confirm whether FluxHealth will consider a 12-month reserved band if we can structure quarterly forgiveness for under-delivery?
- Is the procurement contact copied on this thread the right person for contract/PO discussions?
- Do you have a hard cap on acceptable cold-start latency? We’ve modeled the pricing above with standard low-latency GPUs; deeper quantization/faster kernels change unit economics.

Next steps I recommend:
- Tom: confirm preferred target $/1M token and willingness to entertain a 12-mo committed band.
- Flux procurement: share preferred legal/contracting timeline + PO process link.
- Redwood: I’ll draft a two-slide pricing summary and a short mutual action plan after you confirm the above.

Thanks — Jonas

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0129

From: Tom Barlow <tom@fluxhealth.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FluxHealth economic review & pricing options

Jonas — thanks for the recap and the attachments. This aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Budget: the $2k–$6k/mo was very conservative for the pilot leadership asked to approve; we can flex up to ~$10k/mo if the pilot proves the key metrics.
- Target unit: our preferred target would be ~$50/1M tokens for production-grade SLA. For the pilot we could accept $60/1M if there is a clear path to $45–50 with a commitment.
- Commitment: leadership is open to a 12-month reserved band if there is flexibility on the ramp (i.e., we don’t want to be penalized heavily for a slower-than-expected ramp). Quarterly true-ups would be acceptable.

Procurement is included on this reply (procurement@fluxhealth.ai) — they’ll need the formal pricing worksheet and a draft SOW to scope the pilot work. Also they prefer to see any rebate language and renewal triggers up front.

Two asks for you: can you put together a conservative 12-mo commitment scenario and a low-friction 3mo pilot band that preserves a path to the 12-mo numbers? Also include proposed overage rules and a suggested clause for ramp forgiveness.

—Tom
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: FluxHealth economic review & pricing options

Ben / Marissa — forwarding the external reply. FluxHealth is interested in a 12-mo reserved band but needs ramp forgiveness and prefers quarterly true-ups. They set a target effective unit of ~$50/1M tokens for production SLA, and will accept $60/1M for pilot if pathway to $45–50 exists.

My proposed commercial posture to present to them (short):
- 3mo Pilot band (POC): commit to forecasted mid-case 36M/mo for 3 months at $60/1M tokens. Include 10% free token buffer; overages billed at $75/1M.
- 12mo Reserved option: guaranteed 36M/mo baseline for 12 months at $47.50/1M tokens with quarterly true-ups; under-delivery forgiveness: up to 25% of baseline across the year with ability to roll up to 2 quarters. Overage above baseline billed at $55/1M.
- Renewal incentive: sign a 24-mo renewal within months 9–12 to trigger a one-time 8% rebate on year 1 consumption.

Why this helps Redwood: keeps unit economics acceptable for our Dedicated capacity during ramp and gives FluxHealth a clear path to their target. Margin math: at 36M/mo baseline the blended unit revenue at $47.50 yields acceptable GPU coverage + infra overhead (details in the attached scenario file).

Can you confirm:
1) Ben — do we have authority to approve the $47.50/1M baseline for a 12-mo commit from the AE side, or does this need legal/pricing approval?
2) Marissa — any compliance/legal flags on the renewal rebate clause?

If both green, I’ll send a formal two-page pricing summary and mutual action plan to FluxHealth + procurement (including the SOW ask).

Thanks — Jonas
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: FluxHealth economic review & pricing options

Jonas — that posture is reasonable. Approve $47.50/1M as the baseline for a 12-month reserved band with the quarterly true-up and the 25% annual forgiveness you described. Two caveats:
1) Add explicit language that we reserve the right to convert to a compatible quantized model variant if production SLA requests drop below a defined latency target — we’ll need to capture that in the SOW.
2) Legal should draft the renewal rebate mechanics as a conditional credit (not an up-front discount) to simplify accounting.

Marissa — please flag any compliance issues on the converter clause; if none, Jonas can proceed to send the formal pricing summary to FluxHealth and procurement and attach the draft SOW for their review.

Ben
